newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks recover momentum at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks recover momentum at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks picked up steam after a slow start and closed at session highs Thursday, fuelled by heavy buying in U.S. markets, dealers said.

"The bolsa gained confidence throughout the day, absorbing profit-taking and ending decidedly firm," said Emilio Alessandro of brokers Alessandro. "Tomorrow should also be good because most people are guessing that U.S. employment data will come in line with expectations (Friday)."
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV rose 1.1 percent to 672.17, setting a new record of nearly three years and stretching gains so far this week to 3.1 percent.
Traders attributed the local rise Thursday mainly to Wall Street's bullish reaction to U.S. producer price data.
"Excluding the volatile energy sector, the wholesale inflation numbers were what we expected and boosted sentiment," said analyst Guillermo Girard at Banco Rio.

Oil stocks were the runaway leaders in the session, with Sol Petroleo and Astra rocketing 10 percent and 6.3 percent, respectively, on the back of a steady surge this week in bellwether YPF. The oil giant, boosted by rising world energy prices, rose another 1.7 percent to $27.2 Thursday, taking its gains this week to more than eight percent.

Another top main-tier performer was gas distributor Transportadora de Gas del Sur, which jumped 4.4 percent after Canada's NOVA said it paid $30 million to raise its stake in the pipeline to 19.1 percent from 14.4 percent.

Floor volume remained heavy at 36.1 million pesos compared to 37.5 million Wednesday, while over-the-counter turnover shrank back to normal strong levels of 124.8 million pesos from Wednesday's massive tally of 202.3 million.
The broad market index closed up 0.9 percent, with winners beating losers 37 to 17 and 26 issues closing flat.
MerVal losses were led by pulp and paper maker Celulosa and power utility Capex, off 2.6 percent and 1.2 percent each.
